trace.summary: Both leaders cover the core of chat history: a chat list, search, rename, delete and a not-saved chat mode. ChatGPT also documents pin, archive, locked chats and saving a temporary chat. For Claude, the catalogue shows no chat pin, chat archive or single-chat export. AGI has most of this on web, desktop and mobile. The web run saw search, rename, pin, archive and restore work. The main gaps are no Recently deleted for chats, no locked chats, and thin support in VS Code, Chrome and the CLI.
trace.scope_notes: Claude means the chat product on support.claude.com. Claude Code means code.claude.com and the Claude Code help pages; its sessions (resume, rename, export, archive) are a separate tool. Claude Code on the web and desktop connects to claude.ai sessions, but I treat it as separate. ChatGPT means help.openai.com and chatgpt.com pages. Pages on learn.chatgpt.com describe the new ChatGPT desktop app, which now holds Chat, Work and Codex together, and the Codex CLI and IDE extension. I label each row. Codex rows (resume, fork, thread archive) are the coding tool, not ChatGPT chat. Plan limits seen: Claude chat-search tool is paid plans only; Claude bulk and rename pages list Free to Ultra; Claude retention controls are Enterprise; ChatGPT export is not available in Business or Enterprise workspaces and can take up to 7 days; ChatGPT saved chat history has no cap on any individual plan. All competitor evidence was reviewed 2026-11-22 from the catalogue lines. I did not open the saved pages. AGI web is the only app with person-seen results (W-13 scorecard, 2026-11-24). Everything else is code reading.

capabilities.name: Start a new chat
capabilities.what_it_is: A visible way to open an empty chat with a ready composer, from the app, a shortcut or a widget.

claude.product: Claude (Claude Code /clear starts a fresh session, separate tool)

evidence.says: iOS widget has a button to start a new chat; usage counts toward limits. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Android widget has a new chat button. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Claude Code /clear starts a new empty conversation. Reviewed 2026-11-22.

chatgpt.product: ChatGPT (desktop app docs also cover Codex)

evidence.says: Mobile Home tab is where you start chats and open sidebar history.
Desktop shortcut New chat is Cmd+N or Cmd+Shift+O.
Web sidebar redesign put the new chat button left of the model picker.

requirement.statement: Every app opens an empty new chat with a ready composer. A new chat starts in the mode, model slot and project the user chose, and never silently in another trust boundary.
requirement.source: docs/product/experience-contract.md section 6.1 (Home/new chat); docs/decisions/2026-11-10-founder-decisions.md D-2026-11-10-01 (empty mobile new chat)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Opening a chat costs no model call and no quota. The model shown comes from the catalogue slot (Auto by default). In Local mode a new chat stays on the device with no silent cloud fallback.

current.by_app: All six apps done per ledger.

capabilities.gap: Unsent draft is not restored in the CLI or Chrome (S12.23). No shortcut check was made on every app.
acceptance_criteria: On each app, open a new chat: no prior messages, composer ready.
Type a draft, reload or navigate away, return: draft is back (web, desktop, mobile, VS Code).
Open a new chat while in Local mode: the label still says Local and no cloud call is made.

verification.evidence: Web only: scorecard web.csv W-2 free and subscribed, new chat answered. Other apps: code inspected only.

capabilities.name: Chat list (Recents) with groups, sort and filter
capabilities.what_it_is: A list of past chats, newest first, with pinned chats grouped on top, and options to group or filter.

evidence.says: Single Recents list: quick questions and longer tasks share one conversation list. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Chats are reached from the sidebar or a Chats and tasks page.
Jun 18, 2026: pinned section holds chats and projects; Recents can be one list or grouped by project.
Desktop has one Recents list combining chat and Work, with sort, filter and pin.
Mobile sidebar lists recent chats newest first and syncs across devices.
Saved chat history has no cap on any individual plan.

requirement.statement: One chat list per account, newest first, with a pinned section and an archived view. History is not capped by plan.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The list shows chats from any model or provider and labels the provider where it is not AGI Managed. Reading the list costs no quota. Local and BYOK chats appear only where they are stored (device).

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile built. Chrome, CLI and VS Code have their own session lists. Web filter and group is partial.

capabilities.gap: Filter and group by type, status and last activity is partial (WP247). The archived view still reads Recents (cosmetic, seen). The phone sidebar account row is clipped at 390 wide (seen).
acceptance_criteria: Create three chats, pin one: it shows in a Pinned group above Recents.
Open the list at 390 wide: every row and the account row are fully visible.
Open the archived view: the heading says Archived, not Recents.
Turn off the network: list still shows cached chats and no stale offline banner remains after reconnect.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free and subscribed (Pinned group, Archived view). Defects seen: heading stays Recents in archived view, account row clipped at 390 wide (web-problems-seen-in-browser.csv W-13).

capabilities.name: Search past chats
capabilities.what_it_is: Find an earlier chat by title or message text from a search box or shortcut and open it.

evidence.says: Unified experience limit: search excludes old Cowork tasks, so a search of chats exists but its screens are not described. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Sidebar search finds chats, projects, images and documents; Ctrl+K or Cmd+K opens it on web; filters All, Chats, Images, Documents, Projects.
Search past conversations by keyword from the search bar.
Desktop Search chats can match chat content and Git branch names; no default shortcut.

requirement.statement: A user can search their own chats by title and message text, from every app that keeps history, and open a result. Only chats the user can see are returned.
requirement.source: docs/product/definition.md (Competitive Ecosystem Synthesis Lock: account history searchable); docs/product/experience-contract.md (permission-aware unified search)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Search is a database lookup, not a model call, so it uses no model and no quota. It works whatever model wrote the chat. Local-mode chats are searched only on the device that holds them.

current.by_app: Done on all six apps in the ledger. Mobile search of archived chats is partial.

capabilities.gap: Web shows three result rows for one chat and the dialog jumps as results change (seen, cosmetic). Mobile search of archived chats is partial (MP22).
acceptance_criteria: Search a word that appears in one chat's title: that chat opens from the result.
Search a word that appears only in a message: the chat is found.
Delete a chat, search its title: no result.
Search a word from a temporary chat: no result.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free: search found the chat by title and message text and survived reload; delete removed it from search. Other apps: code inspected only.

capabilities.name: Search scope rules (archived in, deleted and temporary out)
capabilities.what_it_is: Which chats a history search returns: archived included, deleted and temporary chats left out.

evidence.says: Incognito chats are excluded from past-chat search. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Duet search of past chats: deleted chats leave search.
Search matches titles and message text, includes archived chats, and excludes deleted chats.
Locked chats are hidden from sidebar, search, recents and notifications.

requirement.statement: Search honours deletion, revocation, workspace membership, account switching and temporary-chat exclusion. Archived chats are found.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Rules apply to the stored chat, not to the model. On a Local device the same rules apply to local storage.

current.by_app: Web search excludes deleted and temporary rows; archived chats appear only when an Include archived switch is on (off by default).

capabilities.gap: Archived chats are excluded by default on web, unlike the documented ChatGPT behaviour. Needs an owner choice (see unresolved).
acceptance_criteria: Archive a chat, search its title with default settings: result shown, or the include-archived switch is clearly offered.
Delete a chat: not found in search on any app.
Switch accounts: results never show the other account's chats.

verification.evidence: W-13 saw delete leave search; archived search and account switching not recorded.

capabilities.name: Ask the assistant to search earlier chats
capabilities.what_it_is: The assistant itself looks up past conversations on request, or uses them as context, and shows which chats it used.

evidence.says: Claude can search earlier conversations on request, shows citations to source chats with a delete option, and a switch turns it off.
Jan 15, 2026: when enabled, retrieves specifics from past chats and shows the chats used as sources.

requirement.statement: Referencing past chats is a separate, switchable control from saved memory. It shows which chats were used and never reads temporary chats.
requirement.source: docs/product/definition.md (referenced chat history is a separate control; temporary chats neither read nor write memory)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Retrieval is done by AGI, so it must work with any model the user picks. It adds input tokens, so it counts against the one subscription. In Local mode it uses only on-device history.

current.by_app: Not examined here; belongs to the memory page.
evidence: apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:15-17 states temporary chats are left out of the retrieval index

capabilities.gap: Not assessed for this topic.
acceptance_criteria: Turn the reference switch off: the assistant does not cite earlier chats.
Turn it on and ask about a past chat: the answer lists the chat it used.
Ask about a temporary chat's content in a new chat: not found.

verification.evidence: Web W-12 subscribed: recall check could not run because answers failed with a billing error.

capabilities.name: Rename a chat and automatic titles
capabilities.what_it_is: Chats get a title automatically and the user can rename them; the new name persists.

claude.product: Claude (Claude Code /rename is the separate coding tool)

evidence.says: Rename from the three-dot menu on a chat; iOS by long-press; Android from the open chat menu.
Claude Code /rename renames the session or auto-generates a name.

chatgpt.product: ChatGPT desktop app (docs also cover Codex)

evidence.says: Rename chats: give a chat a short outcome title.
Desktop shortcut Rename chat is Cmd+Alt+R.

requirement.statement: A new chat gets a meaningful title automatically. The user can rename it on every app that lists chats, and the name persists.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Auto-title uses a small model call; it must pick a cheap route and must not bill a user's quota visibly more than a reply. In Local mode the title is made on device or left as the first words.

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI done. VS Code and Chrome missing per ledger. CLI /rename is partial.

capabilities.gap: No rename in VS Code (V14); CLI /rename partial (CP30). Web title stays old after an edit of the first message (seen). Title ignores attachments (seen).
acceptance_criteria: Rename a chat, reload: new name stays.
Start a chat by attaching a file: title reflects the content, not a placeholder.
Edit the first message: title updates or stays by a stated rule.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free pass for rename. Defects seen: title stays after first-message edit (W-3), title does not reflect attachments (W-4).

capabilities.name: Pin chats
capabilities.what_it_is: Keep chosen chats at the top of the list.

claude.product: Claude (the catalogue shows starring for projects and pinning for Claude Code sessions, not for chats)

evidence.says: Star projects for sidebar access. This is projects, not chats. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Claude Code agent view: Ctrl+T pins a session (keeps its process alive).
Dec 18, 2025: pin chats to the top; web ... menu then Pin chat; mobile long-press.
Desktop shortcut Pin or unpin chat is Cmd+Alt+P.

requirement.statement: A chat can be pinned and unpinned; pinned chats show together at the top and stay in sync across devices.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Pin is account metadata, free of model cost. It must not move a Local chat to the account.

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile done. CLI, VS Code missing. Chrome missing in ledger but comparison says star exists.

capabilities.gap: No pin in CLI or VS Code. The ledger and the comparison disagree for Chrome.
acceptance_criteria: Pin a chat, reload: it stays pinned in a Pinned group.
Unpin it: it returns to its dated place.
Pin on web: it shows pinned on mobile after sync.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free and subscribed: Pinned group, survived reload.

capabilities.name: Archive and unarchive chats
capabilities.what_it_is: Hide a finished chat from the list without deleting it, and bring it back later.

claude.product: Claude Code sessions only; not documented for Claude chat

evidence.says: Archive a cloud coding session from its menu; find it on the Archived tab and unarchive. Archived sessions cannot take new messages.
Archive a Desktop session; unarchive from the Archived tab.
Archive removes a chat from the sidebar without confirmation; it stays searchable; manage under Settings, Data controls, Archived chats with Unarchive or Delete.
Archive finished chats, or archive all chats in a project; restore from Archived chats in settings.

requirement.statement: A chat can be archived and restored. Archiving never deletes. Archive keeps the chat's provider and Local or Cloud label.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Free of model cost. Local chats archive on the device.

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code done. Chrome missing in ledger, comparison says menu Archive exists.

capabilities.gap: No archive-all for a project (W310). Archiving the open chat leaves it open (seen). Archiving offline gives no feedback (seen).
acceptance_criteria: Archive a chat: it leaves the list and the open view returns to a new chat or says it is archived.
Archive while offline: a clear message, no silent failure.
Restore it: back in the list with its old title and pin state.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free and subscribed: archive, Archived list, restore, survived reload. Defects: offline archive silent, archived chat stays open.

capabilities.name: Archived chats list (restore or delete from it)
capabilities.what_it_is: One place that lists archived chats with open, restore and delete actions.

evidence.says: Archived chats section lists archived chats with dates and project context and restores them.
Settings, Data controls, Archived chats with Unarchive or Delete.

requirement.statement: Settings holds an Archived chats list where each chat can be opened, restored or deleted.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: No model cost. Lists only chats the account or device holds.

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code done; Chrome missing.

capabilities.gap: Chrome has no archived list.
acceptance_criteria: Archive two chats, open the list: both appear with dates.
Restore one: it leaves the list and returns to Recents.
Delete one from the list after a confirm that names what is lost.

verification.evidence: Web W-13: Archived (1) view and Restore worked.

capabilities.name: Delete a chat
capabilities.what_it_is: Remove a chat with a confirmation that says what is lost.

evidence.says: Delete from the three-dot menu with confirmation; the conversation leaves history immediately and is purged from the back end within 30 days.
On Team and Enterprise, deleting removes chats from visible history while backend retention rules still apply.
Delete from the sidebar menu or press-and-hold on mobile; removed from view at once and purged within 30 days.
Clear chat history one by one or all at once; deleted from systems within 30 days.

requirement.statement: Deleting a chat asks first, names the consequence, and removes it from the list and search on every device.
requirement.source: AGENTS.md section 9 (an action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Delete must also remove stored content sent to any provider where AGI controls it, and say where a provider keeps its own copy. Local chats are deleted from the device.

current.by_app: All six apps done per ledger.

capabilities.gap: See the recovery row: the web dialog says it cannot be undone.
acceptance_criteria: Delete a chat: a dialog names the chat and what is lost.
Confirm: chat is gone from list and search on all signed-in devices.
Cancel the dialog: chat is kept.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free: confirm dialog, then gone from list and search. Subscribed run stopped at the dialog.

capabilities.name: Recover a deleted chat (Recently deleted)
capabilities.what_it_is: A deleted chat waits in a recovery area for a period before it is erased for good.

evidence.says: Page only says the chat leaves history at once and is purged within 30 days; it names no user restore. Reviewed 2026-11-22.
Deleted chats are not restorable, even by Support. Reviewed 2026-11-22.

requirement.statement: A chat a user deletes goes to Recently deleted first, can be restored for a stated period, and is then erased. Permanent removal happens only from an explicit action that names what is lost.
requirement.source: AGENTS.md section 9 (a chat or session is archived or moved to Recently deleted)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Applies to every chat AGI stores, whatever model wrote it. Local chats go to a device recovery area.

current.by_app: Server soft-deletes and has a restore route. Support text, CLI privacy text and mobile copy say Recently deleted exists. The web browser run saw no chat recovery area. The Library has Recently deleted for files only.

capabilities.gap: No screen to see or restore a deleted chat. Docs and copy promise one. The ledger marks delete done without checking recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Delete a chat: the dialog says it can be restored for a named number of days.
Open Recently deleted: the chat is listed with days left; Restore returns it to Recents.
After the period, the chat is gone and Search finds nothing.
Delete all chats: the same recovery rule applies, or the dialog says it does not.

verification.evidence: Web W-13 free and subscribed: dialog says 'This cannot be undone'; no Recently deleted area for chats (web-problems-seen-in-browser.csv W-13, minor).

capabilities.name: Select many chats, archive all, delete all
capabilities.what_it_is: Act on several chats at once, or on the whole history.

evidence.says: Web: Select or Select all then Delete. Android: checklist icon enables multi-select with a trash icon.

chatgpt.product: ChatGPT (project archive-all is from the desktop app docs)

evidence.says: Clear chat history one by one or all at once.
A project menu archives all chats in a project together.

requirement.statement: Users can select several chats, and can archive or delete the whole history, each with a confirm that names the consequence. Mobile also deletes all chats in Local mode.
requirement.source: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md D-2026-11-13-01 (deleting all chats in Local mode on mobile); AGENTS.md section 9
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Acts on stored chats of any provider. Local mode deletes on device only and says so.

current.by_app: Web (bulk, archive all, delete all) and mobile (data controls) built. Project-level archive-all missing on web.

capabilities.gap: Archive every chat in a project is missing (W310).
acceptance_criteria: Select three chats and delete: one confirm names the count.
Archive all: all chats move to Archived and none are deleted.
Delete all in Local mode on mobile: only device chats are removed, and the dialog says so.

verification.evidence: Not covered by scorecards or the defect list.

capabilities.name: Temporary chat (not saved)
capabilities.what_it_is: A chat that stays out of history, started from the composer, a menu or a shortcut.

evidence.says: Ghost icon on a new non-project chat starts an incognito chat with a black border; closed with x; not saved to history, memory, training or recap. Unavailable inside projects.
Temporary Chat started from the model menu; not saved in history, uses and creates no memories, not used for training.
Desktop shortcut New temporary chat is Cmd+Shift+N.

requirement.statement: Cloud Chat offers temporary or incognito chat with a visible notice for as long as it is open.
requirement.source: docs/product/experience-contract.md section 7.2 (Cloud Chat composer variants) and section 8 (temporary/incognito notice)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Works with any model on the AGI Managed route. A temporary chat on a BYOK or Local route must say where the content goes. Local-model chats on web and desktop are temporary by decision. Counts against quota like any chat.

current.by_app: Web, desktop, mobile done. CLI conflicting in ledger. VS Code and Chrome missing in ledger; Chrome comparison says it exists.

capabilities.gap: No temporary-chat shortcut on web (comparison row without id). VS Code none. CLI and Chrome unclear.
acceptance_criteria: Start a temporary chat: a banner says so until it is closed.
Send a message, leave, open the list: the chat is not there.
Search a word from it: no result.
Try to share it: a refusal says to turn off temporary chat first.

capabilities.name: What a temporary chat leaves out, and how it is explained
capabilities.what_it_is: The stated rules for history, search, memory, training, files and connectors in a temporary chat, shown on screen.

evidence.says: Incognito chats are kept 30 days by default (or the Enterprise period), appear in Team and Enterprise exports and the Compliance API, and cannot create files or run code in the new experience.
Incognito is excluded from search and memory.
Temporary chats skip history, create no memories and are not used for training while temporary; a safety copy may be kept up to 30 days.
Temporary Chat uploads are not saved to Library.

requirement.statement: A temporary chat stays out of history, search, memory and the Library, keeps no safety copy, and the screen says what a connector or provider may still keep.
requirement.source: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-28-05 (no safety copy); docs/product/definition.md (temporary chats neither read nor write memory)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: AGI cannot erase a copy a BYOK provider or connector keeps; the notice must say so. Local-model temporary chats never leave the device.

current.by_app: Web, desktop done; mobile done except plugin note and kept-output choice.

capabilities.gap: Mobile lacks the plugin note and generated-output saving choice (S41.07, S41.09). A purge job deletes temporary rows after 30 days; whether that conflicts with 'no safety copy' is not checked.
acceptance_criteria: Open the explanation line: it names history, search, memory and Library.
Attach a file in a temporary chat: it is not in Library afterwards.
Use a connector: it asks each time and the screen says the service keeps its own record.
After 30 days no temporary row or attachment remains.

verification.evidence: Not covered by any person-run result.

acceptance_criteria: Start plain: the reply cannot cite saved memory.

trace.summary: Edit, retry, regenerate, response versions, branching and stop are built on Web and Desktop (hosted web app), mostly on Mobile, partly on VS Code, CLI and Chrome. A web tester saw edit with a version pager, stop and regenerate work on 2026-11-24, with defects. Catalogue evidence for the Claude chat product is thin, so most competitor detail is ChatGPT plus the Claude Code and Codex coding tools. Mobile branching conflicts with an owner decision.
trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. ChatGPT (help.openai.com): edit of sent messages incl. image attachments (web Feb 2026; iOS and Android Jun 2026; iOS long-press menu), Branch in new chat (web, Free/Go/Plus/Pro, note dated 2025-09-04), Try again and regenerate with search, retry menu to regenerate with Thinking or Pro (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu), inline retry of failed messages, stop generating (web; macOS shortcut). Claude chat (support.claude.com): only three relevant lines: editing an earlier message makes a separate chat version with its own artifacts (web, desktop); edit and retry when a flagged message pauses the chat (web, desktop, iOS, Android, CLI); and "branching a conversation from an earlier point isn't available" in the unified Cowork and Chat experience. The catalogue has no Claude chat page on retry, regenerate, stop or response versions, so those are has: unknown, not no. Claude Code (code.claude.com plus the support cheatsheet) is a separate coding tool: Esc interrupt, Enter queues a steering message, /rewind and Esc Esc, /branch and --fork-session, fork from an earlier message in the browser (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise), checkpoints in VS Code. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is a separate coding tool: fork a thread from any turn, revert thread history, steer or interrupt a turn, edit or reorder queued messages, fork a chat from an earlier message on desktop. The coding tools connect to the chat products only through shared accounts and Remote Control; their pages are not evidence for chat behaviour. Plan limits: Branch in new chat lists Free, Go, Plus, Pro; the retry menu with Thinking or Pro lists paid plans; Claude Code browser fork lists paid plans.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both document a composer model picker, effort levels, plan-based model access, safety and rate-limit fallbacks, admin model controls and retirement notices. Claude Code and Codex add speed tiers, advisor, plan-then-execute and subagent levels. AGI covers most picker, Auto, effort and fallback items on most apps. Seen by a person on web only: Free has no Auto and the picker hides the active model. Gaps: safety-flag toggle, ultra and ultrafast tiers, admin new-model hold, model recommender.
trace.scope_notes: Reviewed 2026-11-22 from the saved catalogue. Claude (support.claude.com) documents the chat apps: one menu for model, effort and thinking; safety fallback notices; plan notes for the largest model family; context by model. Claude Code (code.claude.com plus support articles about Claude Code) documents /model, /effort, fast mode, advisor, plan-then-execute, fallback chains, subagent models, aliases. The coding tool connects to the chat product through the same account plan and the same safety-fallback setting (Config > Model & Output) and through Remote Control from phone or browser. ChatGPT (help.openai.com) documents the chat picker with Instant, Medium, High, Extra High and Pro levels, plan limits, retirements and Enterprise controls. Codex and ChatGPT Work (learn.chatgpt.com) document a separate model line-up, a Power slider, speed tiers (Fast, Ultrafast), Ultra with subagents, and custom providers. Several newest models appear in Work and Codex but not in regular Chat. Plan limits matter: the largest Claude family is not on Free; the top ChatGPT reasoning option needs Pro or Business; Ultrafast is Pro 500, Enterprise and Edu only. AGI evidence is code reading plus the web scorecard W-6 (one person, one run each for Free and Premium). Model names are left out of this page on purpose; the catalogue owns them.

trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat on web, desktop and phone) documents thinking display, effort, usage-limit and length-limit errors, blocked output and voice interrupts. Its stop, resume and steer controls in the catalogue come from Claude Code (separate coding tool: Esc, Ctrl+C, /btw, --continue) and Cowork. ChatGPT documents stop generating, Regenerate, error messages, thinking levels and early streaming. Steer and queue, interrupt hooks and stream timeouts belong to Codex (separate coding tool). Thinking levels and early streaming depend on plan and model. Review date 2026-11-22. Local-mode behaviour has no leader equivalent.
trace.summary: Streaming states are largely built across the six apps. The project ledger rates 25 of its 29 items done on most apps, and web testers saw streaming and Stop work. Failures a person saw: slow first words (4 to 22 s), the stream lost after a reload mid-answer, a false failure notice after Stop, and silent failure at a credit limit. Gaps: reasoning display in CLI and VS Code, reconnect in CLI and VS Code, and Local-mode checks. Leader evidence for Claude chat controls is thin.
unresolved_product_choices: Whether to add smooth text fade-in while streaming (only ChatGPT is claimed to have it in the comparison; not confirmed here).
Whether to match ChatGPT's early streaming (answer starts before thinking ends) where a provider allows it.
Whether to keep Continue generating, which neither leader is shown to document.
Whether a stopped Cloud run keeps its server-side spend, or the spend is cut at stop (owner rule on billing the partial).
Target first-word time per route and per app, including a Local load-time target.
Whether the CLI and VS Code should show reasoning by default or only on request.
Whether steer or queue is the default while a run is active on each app (web setting exists; CLI uses Enter and Tab in the leader).

trace.summary: Context management splits in two. Claude and ChatGPT chat document context windows, summarising older messages, a context-full notice, upload limits, project retrieval and branching. Claude Code and Codex add manual and tuned compaction and context meters. AGI has server compaction on web and Desktop, with automatic compaction on CLI and VS Code. Gaps: no web context meter, no mobile summary, no manual compact outside CLI and VS Code. No person has seen long-chat behaviour work.
trace.scope_notes: Claude chat (support.claude.com) documents: per-model windows on paid plans, automatic summarising of earlier messages when code execution is on, a length-limit error that differs from the usage limit, project retrieval, and upload limits. Claude Code (code.claude.com plus the Claude Code cheatsheet on support.claude.com) is a separate coding tool. It documents /compact, /context, /clear, /rewind summarise, an autocompact threshold, compaction hooks and a thrash guard. It connects to Claude chat only through shared plans and usage; one page says the ring also shows plan usage shared across Claude Code surfaces. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing) documents window size by plan, a Free-plan context-window-full notice that can start a new chat with a summary, long pastes over 10,000 characters becoming attachments, upload limits, project file limits, and branch in new chat. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com, some help.openai.com pages) is a separate coding tool with manual compaction, tunable auto-compaction, compaction hooks and 272k to 1M windows. Work and Codex share a plan with ChatGPT and have their own larger window. Plan limits matter: Claude's windows and project retrieval are paid-plan items; ChatGPT's window grows from Free to Pro; the full-chat notice is documented for Free. ChatGPT whole-chat compaction is not documented in the catalogue for the chat product, only for Codex; ChatGPT chat has has: unknown there. Memory and cross-chat recall belong to the memory topic and are touched here only where they decide what is sent each turn. Public Desktop is Electron showing the hosted web app, so Desktop chat behaviour is web behaviour; the Tauri code is internal. Competitor review date for all evidence: 2026-11-22. No model names are written here; window sizes are quoted as sizes only.

trace.summary: Both Claude and ChatGPT ship automatic memory, memory controls, custom instructions, and style settings. ChatGPT also has an editable memory summary, memory Sources, tone and trait sliders, and Mac activity memory. Claude has topics, import and export, and a monthly recap. AGI Workforce covers most memory basics in code. Its gaps are goals, units, writing-style learning, memory-used display on mobile and CLI, and capacity limits. Only Free web memory has been seen working by a person.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat product, support.claude.com): memory topics, per-project memory, past-chat search, incognito, import and export, a monthly recap, and account-wide Instructions. Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; on Team and Enterprise the owner controls it. Claude Code (code.claude.com): separate tool with CLAUDE.md files, auto memory, /memory, rules, output styles, and subagent memory. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing): saved memories, chat-history reference, memory summary, Sources, personality presets and trait sliders, and custom instructions of 1,500 characters on Free and Go and 5,000 on paid plans. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com): separate coding tool with local memories (off by default), a global AGENTS.md, and /memories. Computer History on macOS links Codex and ChatGPT, and dots share memory with ChatGPT. Plan and region limits: ChatGPT memory is limited on Free, standard on Go, and expanded on Plus and Pro (chatgpt.com/pricing); chat-history reference is off by default in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein; Computer History is Pro, Business and Enterprise only; Reflect is beta. Review date 2026-11-22. The catalogue shows no Claude chat feature for styles or tones; Claude's output styles appear only for Claude Code.

trace.summary: Both leaders ship Projects: shared instructions, files and sources, project chats, project-scoped memory, and sharing with roles. AGI has most of this on web and desktop, with partial mobile and little in CLI, VS Code and Chrome. A person saw project create, instructions and project chats work on web, and saw file upload fail (likely an unmigrated local database). Main gaps are sources, retrieval, link sharing, import, spend tags and coordinated threads.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (support.claude.com): Projects are workspaces with instructions and knowledge. Free has up to five projects, and paid plans have no cap. Team and Enterprise add sharing with Can view or Can edit. Each project has its own memory with a Use account memory switch. Large knowledge switches to retrieval on paid plans. Claude Cowork (desktop) has a separate kind of project, tied to local folders, with scheduled tasks and memory. Claude Code (code.claude.com) has a beta Projects feature for paid individual plans (Pro, Max, Ultra), not Team or Enterprise. It is one coordinating conversation with parallel cloud threads, one user, no sharing, and a 16,000-character instruction field. It connects to the chat product only through the Claude desktop and web apps; Claude Code CLAUDE.md files are a separate thing. ChatGPT (help.openai.com): Projects are on every plan. Files per project are 5 on Free, 25 on Go and Plus, and 40 on Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu. Sharing exists on all plans, with collaborator caps. Memory can be set to project-only. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com docs): the desktop app's Projects view mixes ChatGPT projects with local folder projects (several folders, one primary). The CLI and IDE treat the open folder as the project and have no Projects view. All catalogue lines were reviewed 2026-11-22. Several Claude and ChatGPT pages describe rollouts, so availability is plan- and account-dependent.

trace.summary: Both leaders take mixed files and images, show per-plan limits, keep a saved-files library and read PDFs, sheets and Office files. AGI already matches most of the web basics: 20 files per message, 500 MiB on paid plans, a Library with storage meter and trash. trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22, catalogue only. Claude (support.claude.com) documents chat uploads, project files, Drive and GitHub knowledge, file creation, Sheets, Cowork local files and Claude in Chrome. Claude Code (code.claude.com and its support FAQ) is a separate coding tool: @path references, Ctrl+V image paste, browser file upload limited to 10 MB, and a Projects page with folder uploads. Its Remote Control saves phone attachments under ~/.claude/uploads, which is where the coding tool meets the chat apps. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing, learn.chatgpt.com use-chatgpt page) documents uploads, Images, Library, Projects, data analysis and per-plan limits. Codex (other learn.chatgpt.com pages) is the separate coding tool: -i image flags, Shift-drag images, and non-image attachments. Plan limits matter: ChatGPT limits differ for Free, Go, Plus, Pro and Business, Library is replacing by Space for some accounts, audio upload is paid only, and Claude project files are capped at 30 MB each. Image generation, Slides and Docs authoring are out of scope except where they touch Library or download. AGI status comes from the comparison CSVs, area briefs 14, 24, 25 and 95, and code. Only the web scorecard and web defect list count as seen by a person.

trace.summary: Claude (artifacts, Docs, Sheets, Design, Data) and ChatGPT (Work files, Pages, Slides, Sites) both document rich generated outputs. AGI's web app has the broadest base: panel, preview, versions, exports, publishing, Sites. Gaps are real sheets with formulas, spreadsheet and slide editing depth, co-editing, Office add-ins, and non-web apps. Only the web Free and subscribed runs show anything working. Excel creation failed in every test. Local-mode behaviour is not documented.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat product, support.claude.com): artifacts are standalone outputs beside the chat. Templates are Docs, Slides, Design, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards and Motion, plus file creation through a sandbox. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is a separate tool. It can publish a private page to claude.ai, with the claude.ai sign-in needed. Those pages appear in the same gallery as chat artifacts (code.claude.com glossary, cc08:4). It is not available on API-key, Bedrock, Vertex or gateway sessions (cc01:187). ChatGPT (help.openai.com, learn.chatgpt.com): Work makes Office files, Pages and Slides live in Space, Sites hosts websites, and older canvas has been removed from newer models for chat (oh08:262). Codex is the separate coding tool; it can also build Sites (cl07:39 says ChatGPT or Codex). The artifacts viewer page (learn.chatgpt.com artifacts-viewer) covers the desktop app, Codex CLI and IDE. Plan limits vary: Claude Docs, Slides and Design are on all plans, Data, Sheets and Whiteboards need Pro or above, Motion is Team and Enterprise only (ch05:136). ChatGPT Sites is Plus and above, and public publishing needs Business or Enterprise. Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. AGI evidence: QA comparison CSVs, area briefs 26-33 and 96, code. The area briefs and comparison CSVs disagree with the code in places (rename, selection edit, comments, deck editing and Google Docs save all exist in apps/web code but briefs mark them missing), so code is used as the higher source. Where I cite the briefs, they are code-reading output, not human observation.

trace.summary: AGI renders the basics (Markdown, tables, code, math, Mermaid, charts, citations, inline interactive cards) on web, desktop and mobile, per code reading. The extensions and CLI trail. Missing: table copy, line numbers, code wrap, news, weather, sports, flights and shopping cards, flashcards, tappable entity panels, inline web images on web. Competitors document visuals and cards, not plain Markdown. No rendering was seen working by a person, except an HTML artifact preview.
trace.scope_notes: Review date 2026-11-22 for all competitor evidence. Claude (chat, support.claude.com): custom visuals (HTML/SVG diagrams, charts, interactive) inline on web and desktop, beta, all users, and not rendered in the iOS or Android apps; artifacts beside the chat; weather and recipe cards on web/desktop. Claude Code (code.claude.com): terminal and editor rendering only (syntax highlight toggle, OSC 8 links, 200-row table cap, LaTeX in the VS Code panel, mods with Markdown/Code/Svg elements); it connects to chat only through shared claude.ai sign-in and artifacts. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing): writing blocks and code blocks with Preview for HTML, React, SVG, Mermaid and Vega; interactive charts; Intelligent UI (layouts, forms, buttons) on a current model generation for all plans; tappable highlights; inline web images. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com): visualizations are not rendered in Codex CLI/IDE; the desktop artifacts viewer previews files; CLI has no preview. Catalogue rows tagged product chatgpt with a learn.chatgpt.com url are the Codex coding tool or its docs. Plan limits: ChatGPT interactive tables and charts are Plus and Pro only on the pricing page, while the release notes and Intelligent UI page list all plans; the two conflict and are not reconciled. Claude Data, Sheets and Motion templates are plan-gated. The catalogue has almost nothing on Claude chat Markdown, code-block copy or table behaviour, so those are unknown, not no.

ChatGPT (help.openai.com) covers chat search, Sources, deep research and shopping; search is available signed out and on Free through Enterprise within usage limits. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is the separate coding tool with cached, indexed, live and disabled search modes. The page learn.chatgpt.com/docs/web-search.md mixes ChatGPT chat and Codex; it is labelled that way below. Plan limits for search call counts are not in the catalogue. Plans: Team and Enterprise owners must enable Claude search; ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu admins toggle it.

trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat) research is documented on support.claude.com. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is a separate coding tool. Plan limits: Claude Research is paid only (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise). ChatGPT deep research is limited on Free and Go, included on Plus, maximum on Pro; Enterprise and Edu have caps; Business, Enterprise and Edu use credits. All competitor evidence was reviewed 2026-11-22 from the catalogue only. AGI evidence is code reading, except web-search runs in the web scorecard.

trace.summary: Tools and code execution: both leaders run sandboxed code, analyse data, make files and ask before app actions. AGI has a wide tool layer on all six apps by code reading. Gaps seen: web code execution awaits a production switch-on, Excel creation failed in the one human web test, and charts, Python-in-canvas, custom connectors and run-code controls are partial or missing. Most items are unverified by a person.
trace.scope_notes: Review date 2026-11-22 for all competitor evidence. Claude (chat) and ChatGPT (chat) are the main references: sandbox code, file creation, data analysis, visuals, connector tools and approval cards. Claude Code (code.claude.com) and Codex (learn.chatgpt.com Codex pages) are separate coding tools. They own shell, OS sandbox, permission modes, hooks and background tasks. They connect to the chat products only in places: Claude Code loads claude.ai connectors when the subscription is the active sign-in (cc07:26), and Codex pages share plugin and Work wording with ChatGPT. Claude Cowork (desktop) is part of the Claude app and adds a VM and computer use. Plan limits seen: Claude code execution and file creation is on for Free through Ultra (ch01:255) but default off on Enterprise (ch03:12). ChatGPT data analysis is in the Free tier (oh09:173). One ChatGPT pricing line limits interactive tables and charts to Plus and Pro (cl08-pr01:58), while a help page lists no plan (oh09:36). Web search, memory, scheduling and artifacts are covered by other topics; only their tool-call display is touched here. Competitor names for specific models are left out on purpose.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both document a connector directory, custom MCP connectors, per-action approvals, skills, plugins and admin controls. ChatGPT has retired custom GPTs in favour of plugins. AGI has most pieces on Web and Desktop, but outside connectors are gated "Coming soon" except 13 named ones. Gaps: custom assistants, multi-account (owner chose one account), tunnels, add-ins, mobile plugins. A person has seen only the Free upgrade path work.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat product, support.claude.com): connectors directory, custom remote MCP connectors, Google and Microsoft 365 connectors, interactive connectors, skills, plugins, org marketplaces. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool: MCP via claude mcp add and .mcp.json with local, project and user scopes, /plugin, SKILL.md, managed MCP. It connects to the chat product by one-way sync of account skills, plugins and connectors (v2.1.273 and later, signed-in account only). ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing): apps now called plugins in Settings > Plugins, permission levels, custom MCP, skills, plugin directory, custom GPTs being retired (11 Dec 2026). Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is the separate coding tool: skills in .agents/skills, app-server apps and marketplaces; it shares the plugin directory with ChatGPT. Plan limits: ChatGPT custom MCP with writes is web-only for Business and Enterprise/Edu; Pro is read/fetch only; Free and Go cannot create plugins or use plugin extensions; Claude Free gets one custom connector; skill sharing, org marketplaces and scanning are Team/Enterprise. ChatGPT skills plan scope differs between pricing page (all individual plans) and the skills help page (Business/Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare). Catalogue rows are from 2026-11-22 pages; review date 2026-11-22.

trace.summary: Both leaders now offer delegated cloud agents (ChatGPT Work and dots, Claude Cowork and Duet), hosted cloud browsers, computer use with per-app permission, and schedules. AGI has Work, schedules, approvals, Desktop computer use on Mac and a Chrome browser agent. It lacks a cloud browser, an always-on agent, subagents outside the CLI, goal loops, and Windows computer use. Only Web was seen by a person; other apps are code-read only.
trace.scope_notes: Evidence read 2026-11-22 from the saved leader catalogue. Claude: Cowork (desktop, web, mobile, Chrome side panel), Claude in Chrome, cloud browser, computer use, Duet (research preview, US waitlist), Claude Tag in Slack. Claude Code is a separate coding tool (code.claude.com) with routines, cloud environments, agent view, teams, workflows and /goal; it connects to chat through the Chrome extension, Desktop and Slack. ChatGPT: Work (cloud or local), cloud browser, desktop built-in browser, Chrome extension, Computer Use, scheduled tasks, workspace agents and dots (always-on cloud agent). Many learn.chatgpt.com pages are shared by ChatGPT Work and Codex (the separate coding tool): subagents, goal mode and automations cover both; CLI and IDE rows are Codex only. ChatGPT agent mode is retired in favour of Work and the cloud browser. Claude Dispatch is closed to new users. Plan limits: ChatGPT cloud browser is paid plans only, Free and Go excluded; dots are Pro tiers, Business Premium and Enterprise, outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, ages 18 and over. Claude cloud browser is Pro, Max and Ultra and not Team or Enterprise; Claude computer use is a preview or beta by plan. Most items are labelled rolling out, beta or preview, so availability varies by account.

capabilities.gap: Chrome panel does not run as a full Work session (S60.01 missing there). Free users get no Work switch and no message (seen on Web). Reloading a finished task showed duplicate rows, scaffold text and a live Start work button. docs/product/requirements.md section 20 says Free Cloud execution is enabled; the plan gate in billing-catalog.ts does not match, and the owner has not settled which holds.
acceptance_criteria: On a paid account, switch to Work, state an outcome, start the run, and receive a result file that downloads.
On Free, the Work entry explains why it is unavailable and offers Upgrade or the waitlist.
Reload a finished task: no duplicated rows and no live Start button.
In Local mode on mobile, Work is hidden or labelled as needing sign-in; no request leaves the device.

capabilities.name: Plan review, questions and approvals during a run
capabilities.what_it_is: The agent shows a plan before acting, can pause to ask a question, and waits for approval of risky steps.

evidence.says: In Manually approve mode the classic panel shows an approvable plan with the sites it will use; the Cowork panel asks Allow all for this website, Allow this time only or Deny (read 2026-11-22).
Plan mode gathers context, asks questions and proposes a step-by-step plan to approve or change (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Before an agent run acts, the user can review and edit the plan; the run pauses for questions and approvals and resumes with the answer.
requirement.source: competitor parity; docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7 requires approval prompts that show action, target, risk and scope
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The plan and approval contract is the same for every model and provider, so a model swap never changes what needs approval. Approval prompts are free of charge and do not consume allowance. In Local mode, approvals gate on-device tools only.

current.by_app: Done on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome for the plan; clarification missing on VS Code.

capabilities.gap: VS Code has no clarification request. A read-only PDF read was labelled high risk when seen on Web.
acceptance_criteria: Start a Work run, see the plan, edit one step, approve, and the run follows the edited plan.
When the agent asks a question, the run stops until you answer, then continues.
Deny an approval and the action does not run.

verification.evidence: Scorecard W-15 subscribed: plan card appeared in about 6 s and two Allow-once approvals worked. Defect: wrong risk label on a read-only read.

capabilities.name: Run progress, steering, pause, stop and retry
capabilities.what_it_is: While a task runs the user sees steps, can redirect it, pause, resume, stop or retry a failed step.

evidence.says: Shows files opened, tools used and choices made, and you can redirect anytime (read 2026-11-22).
Pause halts only the main task; delegated tasks are stopped in Activity and recurring ones in Scheduled; stopping does not undo completed actions (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Every running task can be steered, paused, resumed and stopped, and stopping a run cancels it on the server and says what was already done.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Stop must end metered model calls for any provider at once. A stopped run keeps its usage accounting on the one AGI Subscription. In Local mode, stop halts the on-device model.

current.by_app: Steer and cancel done on all but Chrome (unverified). Pause missing on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. Retry failed step missing on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

capabilities.gap: Pause and retry are missing on several apps. Stopping an answer raised a false Agent run failed bell notification, and a stopped run showed every step in red.
acceptance_criteria: Press Stop on a running task: no further steps or charges appear after 20 seconds, including after a reload.
Pause a task, resume it, and it continues from the same step.
Stop raises no failure notification.

verification.evidence: W-15 subscribed: Stop halted cleanly. W-1 free defect: Stop creates an Agent run failed notification. W-15 subscribed defect: stopped run shows red error icons.

capabilities.name: Long-running work that continues when the device is off
capabilities.what_it_is: A task runs on the provider's servers, keeps going when the app is closed, and can be followed from another device.

evidence.says: Cloud sessions run on Anthropic servers, follow the account across devices and keep working while away; local files, browser and computer need the desktop app open (read 2026-11-22).
Work uses its own browser on a separate cloud computer and keeps working when you close your device (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Cloud tasks keep running when the user's device is off, show live progress, and notify on completion or when input is needed.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Server runs are metered on the one AGI Subscription and need an entitlement check at start and a limit stop mid-run. Anything that needs the user's device (local files, browser) is labelled as device-bound and waits when the device is offline. Local mode runs nothing on servers.

current.by_app: Cloud tasks exist on Web, Desktop and Mobile; Cloud coding tasks failed in testing.

capabilities.gap: On Web the first turn of every new cloud coding task was cancelled and no live progress showed (W-18).
acceptance_criteria: Start a cloud task, close the app, and a completion notification arrives with the result.
Progress is visible while the task runs.
With the paired computer offline, a device-bound step says so and waits instead of failing silently.

verification.evidence: W-18 subscribed (blocked): first turn of each new cloud task cancelled within about 1 s; no live progress; Run this task again then completed. Defects in web-problems-seen-in-browser.csv.

capabilities.name: Choose where a task runs
capabilities.what_it_is: The user picks cloud or their own computer for a task, and the product explains the difference.

evidence.says: Local files, browser use and computer use reach your machine only through Desktop; from Oct 6, 2026 new Pro, Max and Ultra tasks always run in the cloud and an Only on your computer choice was removed (read 2026-11-22).
Without local access, Local suits tasks needing the computer and Cloud suits ones such as scheduled website checks (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: The user sees where each task runs (device, AGI cloud, outside service) and can choose it where both exist; a task never moves across a trust boundary without consent.
requirement.source: docs/product/definition.md and AGENTS.md section 6 (explicit execution boundaries; Local to cloud only by explicit consent)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: On-device runs use the local model or BYOK key and do not draw cloud allowance; cloud runs use the one AGI Subscription. Local mode never falls back to cloud silently; a move is an explicit fork with a visible label.

current.by_app: Desktop done; Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome missing the choice.

capabilities.gap: Only Desktop offers the choice. The Web Your computer page needs a paired Desktop link; the phone cannot add a file to a computer session.
acceptance_criteria: On Desktop, start the same task on this computer and in the cloud; the task card shows which one ran it.
On Web, pair a computer and send a task; the page shows where it runs.
Take the paired computer offline: the run reports offline instead of hanging.

verification.evidence: Comparison rows WP124, DP35 and ledger S60.07. No scorecard step covers it.

capabilities.name: Parallel subagents and background agents
capabilities.what_it_is: One request splits into several agents working at once, with their own context, results and status.

evidence.says: Five ways to run work in parallel: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows and projects; chat Cowork also coordinates sub-agents (read 2026-11-22).
Cowork coordinates sub-agents and delivers finished files (read 2026-11-22).
In ChatGPT Work agents run in the hosted environment and the chat shows their activity; the subagents panel is read-only (read 2026-11-22). Custom agent files and CLI commands are Codex.

requirement.statement: A parent task can delegate to child agents, and the user can see each child, its role, status, result and cost.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Each child can run on a different model or provider, chosen by the routing registry, and each child's cost is recorded on the one AGI Subscription with a cap on parallel children. In Local mode children run on the local model and only as many as the device can hold.

current.by_app: CLI done (cap fixed at 7); VS Code partial; Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome missing.

capabilities.gap: Cloud Work and Desktop run as one agent; no delegation or child list on Web, Desktop or Mobile; CLI limits are fixed constants.
acceptance_criteria: On CLI, start a task that spawns subagents and see each one listed with role and state.
On Web Work, a task that delegates shows each child's result separately.
The child count never exceeds the plan concurrency limit.

verification.evidence: Ledger S62 and comparison rows; no scorecard step covers subagents.

capabilities.name: Goal loop with a completion condition
capabilities.what_it_is: The user states a completion condition and the agent keeps working, checking the condition after each turn, until it is met or judged impossible.

evidence.says: A condition up to 4,000 characters; a fast model checks it after each turn; works in the CLI and Desktop; shows turns and token spend (read 2026-11-22).
Typing /goal in desktop, CLI or IDE starts a goal whose text is both first prompt and completion criteria; goals keep the same sandbox and approvals (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: A task can carry an explicit completion condition that the agent checks before finishing, with a visible budget.
requirement.source: competitor parity in the coding tools only; docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md says features neither leader offers are not built, but both offer this one
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The condition check is a small extra model call on the same subscription and must count against allowance. It must work with any model and stop on limit. In Local mode the check runs on the local model.

current.by_app: Missing on every app.

capabilities.gap: No /goal, no completion condition, no time budget. Spend budget exists only on the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Set a goal; the run continues across turns and stops with a reason when met.
A goal that cannot be met ends with an impossible verdict and a reason.
A spending cap ends the run.

capabilities.name: Always-on personal agent
capabilities.what_it_is: A persistent agent that follows up between conversations, delegates in the background, and reaches out with results.

evidence.says: Message Claude like a person; it runs on its own cloud computer, keeps working after the app closes, and sends a morning brief; no model choice, cannot take over its browser (read 2026-11-22).

Always-on cloud agent that runs even when your computer is off, uses background agents and reaches out with results; Pro tiers, Business Premium, Enterprise; ages 18 and over outside EEA, UK, Switzerland (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Not decided; if built, an always-on agent runs only in Managed Cloud, shows its own rules for acting without asking, and can be paused or deleted.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: It must route per task across providers, charge background work to the one AGI Subscription with a visible cap, and never exist in Local mode, which has no cloud runtime.

current.by_app: Missing on Web and Mobile; scheduled tasks and event triggers are the nearest.

capabilities.gap: No persistent agent, roster, presence, daily brief or per-agent rules. Roster items S61.* are done only in the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Not applicable until the owner decides.

capabilities.name: Custom and workspace agents
capabilities.what_it_is: Users or teams build named agents with instructions, tools and schedules, share them, and start them from chat, Slack or an API call.

evidence.says: Plugins bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents, saved to the account and used in chat, Claude Code and Cowork (read 2026-11-22).
Build from template or conversation, preview, schedule, API trigger that returns 202 with a conversation URL, run by @ mention, version history, analytics (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Users can build, version, share and trigger custom agents; an agent can only use the connectors and actions its owner allowed.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: An agent stores a model preference or Auto and runs on any provider; its runs and API triggers are metered on the owner's AGI Subscription. Local mode can run an agent only with on-device tools.

current.by_app: Web Agents page builds, versions and publishes; mobile lists and edits. Persistent roster items are CLI only.

capabilities.gap: No @ mention to run an agent in any chat, no duplicate, no per-action limits in each connector, no admin switch for who may build or publish.
acceptance_criteria: Create an agent, restrict it to one connector, run it, and see the other connectors refused.
Start an agent run by an API call with a scoped token.
Restore an earlier agent version.

verification.evidence: Comparison rows; no scorecard step covers agents.

capabilities.name: Scheduled tasks and monitoring
capabilities.what_it_is: Prompts that run once or on a repeat, in the cloud, with run history, notifications and tasks that watch for changes.

evidence.says: Hourly, daily, weekly, weekdays or on demand; each run is its own session; runs remotely even with the computer off; a Scheduled page to pause, resume, run now, edit (read 2026-11-22). Claude Code has separate cloud routines, desktop schedules and /loop.
One-time, recurring and monitoring tasks that notify on changes and stop at an end condition, managed from a Scheduled page (read 2026-11-22).
evidence.plans: Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu

requirement.statement: Users create, run now, pause, edit and delete schedules; runs ask for approval when needed; missed runs are explained.
requirement.source: docs/product/requirements.md section 20 (cloud routine, run history, pause, resume, delete, notification, permission review)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: A schedule stores a model or Auto and works on any provider; each run is metered on the one AGI Subscription, with plan caps on active schedules owned by billing-catalog.ts. A run held by an exhausted allowance should wait for the reset. In Local mode only local desktop schedules on this computer apply.

current.by_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome have it. Schedule cap by plan; Free has none.

capabilities.gap: Missing: pause until a date, duplicate, deferred run after allowance reset, connection-expiry repair, team shared tasks, scheduling from inside a chat, publishing an artifact from a run. Per-routine effort (S63.10) was ruled not to be built by D-2026-09-27-02, yet cc16:102 in the leader catalogue shows Claude Code routines choose effort.
acceptance_criteria: Create a one-time schedule; it runs once and shows Completed, not Paused.
On Free, Scheduled shows an Upgrade or waitlist path and no create control.
A recurring schedule shows next and last run.
A schedule waiting for approval shows Approve and Deny.

capabilities.name: Event-triggered tasks
capabilities.what_it_is: A task starts when something happens in a connected service (new email, Slack message, pull request, webhook).

Tasks run on new Gmail mail, Slack channel messages or GitHub pull request activity, with Trigger, Condition and Prompt; approvals may pause them (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: A task can start from a connected-service event or a signed webhook, with filters, and obeys the same approvals as other runs.
requirement.source: docs/product/requirements.md section 20 (automations) and ledger S63.15 to S63.17

capabilities.gap: Triggers cover GitHub, Slack and webhooks fully; events from other connected apps are not covered.
acceptance_criteria: Post a signed webhook; a run starts and appears in history.
A filter that does not match starts no run.
An event run that needs approval pauses until approved.

verification.evidence: Comparison row WP123; no scorecard step covers triggers.

capabilities.name: Cloud coding agents and environments
capabilities.what_it_is: Coding tasks run in a hosted environment with repositories, network access level and secrets, reachable from phone and web.

evidence.says: Each cloud session runs in an environment with configurable network access, variables, network secrets and a setup script; used by desktop, mobile, web and CLI (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The coding agent uses any capable model; sandbox time and tokens count on the one AGI Subscription. Secrets are never shown to the model. Local mode uses the local developer host instead.

current.by_app: Web Code page and CLI cloud sessions exist; saved environments, secrets and the CLI environment picker are missing.

capabilities.gap: Each session gets one network level and no secrets. No self-hosted runners.
acceptance_criteria: Start a cloud coding task on a repository and receive a branch or pull request.
Set network access to none and confirm the task cannot fetch a URL.
Cancel the task and see no further commits.

capabilities.name: Delegating from Slack
capabilities.what_it_is: Tag the assistant in a Slack channel to delegate work; it replies in thread with progress and can follow up.

evidence.says: Tag @Claude in Slack channels to do work; it keeps channel context, schedules follow-ups and checks in proactively (read 2026-11-22).
Code and Chat routing modes start a Claude Code session from a mention (read 2026-11-22).
Add the agents app to a channel, connect an agent with its own handle, and choose reply to every message or only on mention (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Mentioning the assistant in Slack starts a run under the channel's tools and approvals, with approve and cancel in Slack.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Slack text is untrusted input. Runs use the workspace's AGI Subscription allowance and any provider. Not available in Local mode.

current.by_app: Web settings; Slack tasks run Work, not coding sessions.

capabilities.gap: No coding session from Slack, no standing digests or channel watching, no Linear triage hand-off.
acceptance_criteria: Mention the assistant in a channel and receive an in-thread result.
A run needing approval posts Approve and Deny buttons.
A channel set to off ignores mentions.

verification.evidence: Comparison rows; no scorecard step covers Slack.

capabilities.name: Approval modes and per-tool permission levels
capabilities.what_it_is: The user chooses whether the agent asks for every action, only risky ones, or none, and sets permission per tool or connector.

evidence.says: Manual asks before each action, Auto reviews each action with a safety check, Skip does no checks; connector tools can be Always allow, Needs approval, Always ask or Blocked (read 2026-11-22).
App permissions choose when ChatGPT asks: Always ask, Any changes, Important actions or Never ask; some high-risk actions can still be blocked (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: Three approval modes plus per-tool Allow, Ask or Deny, enforced in a tool-call gate; some actions always ask in every mode.
requirement.source: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7 and section 21.4 (high-impact confirmations, no sensitive action without approval)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The gate runs outside the model so no provider can bypass it. An automatic safety check must not bill the user separately without disclosure. In Local mode the gate applies to on-device tools.

current.by_app: Same on Web, Mobile and Chrome; Chrome Auto and Full access are partial against the leaders' wording.

capabilities.gap: No notice when Auto is on in Chrome; no free-text standing rules; no per-chat approval for sending messages.
acceptance_criteria: Set Ask before every action; every tool call prompts.
Set a connector tool to Deny; the agent cannot call it.
Changing a permission setting asks in every mode.

verification.evidence: W-15 subscribed: Allow-once approvals worked. Other modes: code inspected only.

capabilities.name: Cloud browser for the agent
capabilities.what_it_is: The agent uses its own hosted browser on a server, so it can read, click and type on sites while the user's device is off.

evidence.says: Claude browses in a server-side browser shown as a card in chat; not on Free, Team or Enterprise (read 2026-11-22).
Work gets its own remote browser to read pages, click and fill forms; it keeps running after the user leaves and pauses for input, sign-in or confirmation (read 2026-11-22).

current.by_app: Missing on Web and Mobile; Desktop has none either.

capabilities.gap: Cloud Work only uses search and page reading. No hosted browser, site settings, cookie list or card in the task.
acceptance_criteria: Not applicable until the owner decides; if built, a cloud task opens a page, fills a form and shows a replay.

If blocked you can take control of Work's computer on mobile and desktop (read 2026-11-22).

requirement.statement: The user can take over a running browser or computer task, then hand back without ending the run.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Control handoff is local logic, independent of provider. While the user holds control the model is not called. Local mode can offer it on the same computer.

current.by_app: Chrome and Desktop computer use done; Web, Mobile, CLI and VS Code missing; Chrome side panel hand back works.

capabilities.gap: S64.23 and S64.24 are missing on every app including Chrome; the Chrome extension row is listed Same elsewhere. No take over for a cloud browser.
acceptance_criteria: Take over mid-task, type input, hand back, and the task resumes.
If control is not handed back in time the task ends with a clear message.
Stop ends everything.

requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Credentials must be kept out of any provider payload, as for BYOK disclosure. The pause is free. Local mode keeps all sign-ins on the device.

capabilities.gap: No secure sign-in form, no saved login with confirmation, no password manager.
acceptance_criteria: At a sign-in page the agent stops and asks you to sign in; after you finish it continues.
At a CAPTCHA the agent asks you and never tries to solve it.
The typed password is absent from the model transcript.

Clear browsing data removes cookies and sign-ins.
A blocked site is refused.

trace.summary: Both leaders ask before risky actions and let users pick how often. AGI's ledger (area 59) marks most approval basics done on all six apps from code reading. One web run showed Allow once working. Main gaps: model-judged auto approval, per-site browser rules on mobile and desktop, editing a proposed action, named permission profiles, admin limits, and wallet or financial confirmation. Nothing else is seen working by a person.
trace.scope_notes: Review date 2026-11-22. Claude (chat, Cowork, Claude in Chrome, Duet) is documented on support.claude.com. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool; it reaches the chat product through Desktop code sessions, cloud sessions and shared Chrome. ChatGPT is documented on help.openai.com and learn.chatgpt.com (apps, cloud browser, dots, Work). Codex is the separate coding tool, documented on learn.chatgpt.com and help.openai.com; it shares computer-use and plugin permissions with ChatGPT desktop. The catalogue labels both ChatGPT and Codex as chatgpt, so each capability below names which one the page covers. Many Claude and ChatGPT items are plan-gated (Claude Chrome and Cowork: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise; ChatGPT cloud browser: paid plans; some dot and Work items: Business or Enterprise), and several are beta, preview or rolling out. Documentation availability is not account availability. AGI status below comes from the QA ledger and comparison files (code reading), not from live runs, except where stated.

trace.summary: Both leaders document live spoken conversation, dictation, voice and language settings, and voice privacy. ChatGPT goes further on voice (files, plugins, background, CarPlay, translation, voice-driven work, plan hours). Claude adds a coding-tool dictation set. AGI has live voice, dictation and read aloud on web, desktop, mobile and Chrome, but live voice is cloud-only and tied to one managed provider. Gaps: VS Code, push-to-talk on web, screen share, background voice, admin switches, translation, meetings.
trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22 (catalog ids cited as ch/cc/cl/oh numbers). Claude (support.claude.com) documents voice mode (beta, all plans; web, Desktop, iOS, Android), mobile dictation, Quick Entry dictation on Mac, and meetings. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is a separate tool: /voice push-to-talk dictation in the CLI, a mic button in the VS Code extension, claude.ai sign-in required (no API key, Bedrock, Vertex or gateway), not in cloud, SSH or VS Code Remote sessions; the chat product's own page says Cowork and Claude Code get dictation only, not voice conversation (ch01:124). ChatGPT (help.openai.com) documents the live voice experience, dictation and Record. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is the separate coding tool; its voice pages (voice chat hotkey, voice that starts and checks tasks, appshot screen context, Micro Mic key) sit inside the ChatGPT desktop app's Chat, Work and Codex, so they are marked ChatGPT and Codex. Plan limits matter: ChatGPT voice has rolling 24 hour limits by plan (oh05:52) and older voice modes retire on Dec 11, 2026; Claude voice counts toward normal plan limits (ch01:121); Claude Code dictation needs Pro, Max, Ultra or Team/Enterprise via claude.ai and does not use tokens (cc21:158). The catalogue shows no Claude read-aloud feature and no Claude voice limits table, so those are unknown, not absent. The comparison CSVs sometimes say Claude has a feature the catalogue does not show; this page follows the catalogue. AGI status comes from code reading (comparison README, snapshot 2026-11-22), and the ledger briefs (areas 48-50) are sometimes older than the comparison rows; conflicts are named per capability. Nothing is seen working by a person except the web voice basics W-10 (scorecard and defect file).

trace.summary: Reviewed 2026-11-22. ChatGPT documents image input, generation, editing and a library. It also documents GIFs, stickers and provenance marks, and its Sora video product has been shut down. Claude documents image input only. It says it makes no photos or video, only code-built visuals and animations. AGI has image and video generation on web, but mobile video is switched off. AGI has no undo or redo, brushes, templates, sketch input or provenance checker, and a person saw Free image generation fail. Local-mode image behaviour is not established.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (support.claude.com): reads images and PDFs, and draws diagrams, charts and interactive visuals as code. It says it does not make photos, illustrations, photorealistic image or video (can-claude-produce-images page; child-safety page). Claude Motion makes code-built animations and MP4 export, with no video model and no realistic footage; it is listed for Team and Enterprise. Claude Code (code.claude.com plus support pages on it) is the separate coding tool: image paste and drag only. Its chat link is the Chrome extension and Claude apps, which accept screenshots. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, chatgpt.com/pricing): image input, image creation and editing, library, GIF, stickers, try-on, provenance marks. Plans: vision limited on Free, standard on paid; image generation limited on Free, included on Go, Plus and Pro; Thinking-assisted images Plus and Pro only. Sora web and app shut down 2026-04-26 and its API 2026-09-24. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com/docs) is the separate coding tool and the Work desktop surface: --image input, an image-generation skill that burns included limits 3 to 5 times faster, and a Canvas image viewer. Codex pages are labelled Codex below. Evidence gaps: surfaces and plans are often blank in the catalogue. Claude pages rarely state per-plan image limits. Review date for all competitor claims is 2026-11-22.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both run coding in a cloud agent, open pull requests and review them on GitHub. Both keep this in separate coding tools (Claude Code, Codex) linked from the chat apps. AGI has a web Code tab, desktop, phone, CLI and VS Code sessions, and a GitHub review pipeline. No person has seen a pull request opened. The web Code tab was seen failing once and blocked once. Main gaps: review rules, auto-fix, environments, handoff.
trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. Four products are kept apart. Claude is the chat product: files and code execution, artifacts, a GitHub read integration (support.claude.com). Claude Code is the separate coding tool (code.claude.com) in terminal, IDE, desktop Code tab and on the web at claude.ai/code. Its cloud sessions start from claude.ai, the Claude mobile app Code tab, the Desktop app and the CLI, and share plan limits with Claude chat. ChatGPT is the chat product: code blocks, Python run, a read-only GitHub connector, Work with Apps on macOS. Codex is the separate coding tool (learn.chatgpt.com and help.openai.com Codex articles) with app, CLI, IDE, cloud tasks and Code Review. It is reached from the ChatGPT apps (the desktop menu picks ChatGPT or Codex; mobile has cloud tasks and a Remote tab) and is covered by ChatGPT plans. Plan limits seen in the catalogue: Claude Code cloud sessions need Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise and are blocked under zero data retention, HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys. Claude managed Code Review is Team and Enterprise only, GitHub only, billed as usage credits apart from plan usage. Ultrareview is a research preview with three free runs on Pro, Max and Ultra. Claude Tag in Slack is Team and Enterprise beta. Codex cloud is on paid ChatGPT plans; @ChatGPT in Slack is Business and Enterprise; GitLab is beta. One Codex page says legacy cloud still powers Code Review and Security Review during a transition. AGI side: the web Code tab is paid-only (a Free account sees an Upgrade and waitlist path). Cloud sessions need the managed sandbox gate (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION plus E2B_API_KEY, apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:16-30). Local sessions run through the CLI-hosted developer runtime on the device. AGI statuses come from code reading unless a row says a person saw it.
