trace.scope_notes: Claude chat (Cowork, claude.ai apps) offers scheduled tasks via support.claude.com. Claude Code (code.claude.com) has three separate paths: cloud scheduled tasks (formerly routines, with schedule, API and GitHub triggers), desktop local tasks, and in-session /loop. Cloud tasks need a claude.ai account and paid plans. ChatGPT has Scheduled tasks on web and mobile (help.openai.com): Free gets 3 active, one-time or daily at most; event triggers need Plus or higher and an admin switch in managed workspaces. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) has desktop automations with local projects and worktrees; CLI and IDE have no Scheduled interface. Dots are a rolling-out ChatGPT feature. The coding tools connect to the chat products through shared account and plan usage. Review date 2026-11-22.
trace.summary: Both leaders ship scheduled tasks: recurring and one-time, run history, notifications, event triggers and plan caps. Claude Code adds local, cloud and in-session loops; ChatGPT adds monitoring, sharing and in-chat schedules. AGI has a broad Cloud-only version on most apps, seen working once on Web for a one-time run. Local scheduled tasks and in-session loop are not built. Several Web defects were seen.
unresolved_product_choices: Whether to match ChatGPT-only features: share task by link on Mobile, monitoring on Mobile, schedule inside an existing chat, always-on dots.
Whether to match Claude Code-only features: /loop, combined schedule plus event triggers, scheduled artifact publishing, token-managed API trigger UI, CI scheduling.
Whether Local scheduled tasks use the device only while the app is open, or also a background service.
Whether a run blocked by the usage allowance is held and run after reset or skipped.
Whether team shared tasks are in scope for the first release.
Whether per-task notification settings stay web-only or become account-wide as the owner decision says.

trace.summary: Both leaders tell users when work finishes or needs them through OS alerts, phone push, email, an in-app bell, terminal bells and hooks. AGI has web, desktop, mobile and Chrome alerts, a bell, quiet hours and break reminders. CLI and VS Code have little. Missing: SMS, per-project mute, event-type filters, agent-sent pushes, inline reply. A person saw the web bell fail twice (wrong or false entries). Delivery on other apps is code-read only.
trace.scope_notes: Reviewed 2026-11-22 from the catalogue. Claude (support.claude.com, claude.com) covers: Cowork phone notification when a task finishes or needs input (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise), usage credit alerts, break reminders and quiet hours (beta), Chrome extension notifications, Duet morning brief (preview), and Slack tag-back (Team, Enterprise, beta). Claude Code (code.claude.com) is a separate tool and carries most of the detail: terminal channels, Notification hooks, Remote Control phone pushes (needs Remote Control and Anthropic infrastructure; unavailable on third-party providers), the PushNotification tool, desktop OS alerts for Code sessions, and per-project notification choices. Claude Code connects to Claude through Remote Control, Dispatch and Cowork pushes to the Claude phone app. ChatGPT (help.openai.com) covers scheduled-task push and email, the Mac app background-reply alert, safety notices to parents and trusted contacts, and meeting reminders (Pro, Business, beta). Pages on learn.chatgpt.com (desktop settings, activity bell, pet, dots, webhooks) describe the desktop app and the Codex tool without always separating them; Codex pages (TUI notifications, notify program, app-server) are the coding tool. Dots are rolling out, some Pro (U.S.) beta. Several rows are rolling out or preview. Whether a limit-reset notification exists at either leader is not in the catalogue.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both share chats as snapshot links, share artifacts and projects with roles, and manage links centrally. ChatGPT adds Teams, Spaces and Pages with live co-editing and project links. Claude adds artifact comments and email invites to chats. AGI has chat links, project roles and artifact audiences on web, and a person saw chat share and revoke work. Co-editing, teams, named-person chat shares and artifact comment roles are missing.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat product, support.claude.com): chat snapshot links, named-person chat invites, project sharing (Team, Enterprise), artifact sharing with roles, Docs, Sheets and whiteboard co-editing. Claude Code (code.claude.com): cloud session sharing (Private/Team) and artifact comments that a Claude Code session answers; these connect to the chat product through shared artifacts at claude.ai. ChatGPT (help.openai.com, learn.chatgpt.com): conversation links, project sharing for all plans, Teams, Spaces and Pages, Sites, Library sharing, workspace agents. Codex: read-only snapshot share of a coding chat (Codex pages are the coding tool). Plan limits matter: Claude public chat links are on Free to Ultra and not on Team or Enterprise; named-person chat shares, org sharing and project sharing are Team or Enterprise; ChatGPT Teams, Library sharing and Sites co-editing are Business or Enterprise; project sharing in ChatGPT covers individual plans with collaborator caps. ChatGPT group chats were retired on 2026-07-09. All competitor facts are from the 2026-11-22 catalogue, reviewed 2026-11-22. AGI status comes from code reading in the comparison files plus one human run (web scorecard W-14).

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both keep chats and cloud work on the account across web, desktop and phone. Both let a phone steer work on your own computer, but only in their coding tools (Claude Code, Codex). AGI has account sync built on web, mobile and CLI. Mobile Remote Control and Dispatch are off in v1. Gaps: hand off between hosts, Apple Handoff, send local session to cloud (desktop), admin and trusted-device controls. No person has tested sync across two devices.
trace.scope_notes: Division of the topic (evidence reviewed 2026-11-22). Claude (chat product, support.claude.com): account sign-in on web, desktop and phone; conversations carry over (documented for the Education page); log out of all sessions; Cowork cloud sessions follow the account and keep running with the laptop closed; the Chrome side panel saves chats that reopen on other devices. Claude Code (code.claude.com, separate coding tool): Remote Control from phone or browser to a session on your own machine, teleport of a cloud session into the terminal, /desktop hand-off, send a Desktop session to the cloud, Dispatch (phone to Desktop, marked deprecated and not available to new users). Claude Code connects to the Claude chat product through the same account, the Claude phone app Code tab and claude.ai/code. ChatGPT (chat product, help.openai.com and chatgpt.com): chat history syncs across devices; one subscription on all devices; log out of one or all sessions; Cloud Work chats sync across web, mobile and desktop; local Work stays on the computer; Apple Handoff between iPhone and Mac (macOS release notes). Codex (separate coding tool, learn.chatgpt.com and some help.openai.com pages): remote connections from the ChatGPT phone app or another desktop to a host computer, QR pairing, hand off a chat between hosts, SSH hosts. Codex connects to ChatGPT through the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps (Codex tab or Remote tab) and the same account. Plan limits: Claude Code Remote Control lists Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise. Claude Cowork cloud lists Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise. ChatGPT Work local sync lists Enterprise and Business (one page) and Paid plans (another). Several ChatGPT remote features are marked rolling out or preview. The catalogue is the only competitor source; any behaviour it does not show is marked unknown. AGI's own rules: two continuity domains (Account Cloud, and Host developer), nothing crosses without an explicit provenance-preserving handoff, Local chats are never synced silently, and Remote Control comes with paid plans only (owner decision 2026-10-22).

trace.summary: Settings competitor evidence reviewed 2026-11-22 for general, appearance, language, data controls and shortcuts. AGI's web, desktop and mobile settings are mostly built by code reading. Only theme and archive were seen working by a person (web). Main gaps: only English and Spanish selectable, no time zone, no chat-history import, no editable shortcuts on mobile, no local-data wipe on desktop, and VS Code and Chrome lag the other apps.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (support.claude.com) documents Settings > Appearance (color mode, chat font), a profile-menu Language choice, Settings > Privacy (export, shared chats) and Delete account. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool: /config, /theme, /keybindings, language and reduced-motion keys, screen reader mode. Where its app is Desktop's Code tab, theme colors come from a mod, so it connects to the chat app only there. ChatGPT (help.openai.com) documents Settings > General (theme, accent, language, text size on Windows), Data controls (improve the model, export, archive all, delete all), Notifications and Delete account. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is the separate coding tool: Settings has a keyboard shortcut editor, Appearance with theme sharing, archived chats, follow-up behavior and import from other coding tools. Plan limits seen: Claude export is for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Team and Enterprise members need an owner switch; Claude dictation languages are beta; ChatGPT export and delete-account are not self-service in Business or Enterprise; ChatGPT improve-the-model default is on for Free, Plus and Pro. No Claude chat page in the catalogue documents rebinding chat shortcuts, a text-size setting, or an accent color. Evidence date for all competitor claims: 2026-11-22. AGI statuses come from code reading (ledger areas 84, 85, 11 and the comparison CSVs), not from running the apps. Several comparison rows have no list_id; those are named by their feature text.

trace.summary: Privacy and data controls: 29 capabilities compared with Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT and Codex pages saved 2026-11-22. AGI is ahead on opt-in training switches, voice audio, and recoverable deletion (code reading only). Gaps: locked chats, retention schedule text, CLI and extension controls, HIPAA and zero retention, cloud browser data. No privacy settings were run by a person. One live finding contradicts the recovery claim.
trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. Claude (support.claude.com): consumer training choice, incognito chat, memory controls, export, account deletion, sessions, voice audio, Enterprise retention, CMEK, US-only inference, Compliance API. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool: local transcript retention, purge, telemetry opt-outs, sandbox, HIPAA setup. Its consumer data-usage page links it to the chat product: Free, Pro, Max and Ultra choose training at the claude.ai privacy controls and Claude Code follows (cc05:241, cc05:245). ChatGPT (help.openai.com): training toggle, Temporary Chat, Locked chats, Privacy Center, export, deletion, MFA, passkeys, Advanced Account Security, Lockdown Mode, active sessions, residency, EKM. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) is the separate coding tool: history persistence, Computer History (local, 48-hour events, clearable), approvals; its training preference is set in ChatGPT Data controls (oh08:49, help.openai.com). Many controls are plan-limited: training toggle is Free, Plus, Pro only; retention, residency, CMEK, Compliance API and HIPAA are Enterprise, Edu or Healthcare; export and deletion are not self-serve for Business or Enterprise. Claude MFA, passkeys, Lockdown and locked chats do not appear in the catalogue, so Claude is unknown there, not no. AGI ledger statuses and comparison rows come from code reading; a person has seen only memory (W-12) and sharing (W-14) work on web, and saw chat delete with no recovery (W-13). Desktop public app shows the hosted web app, so its code evidence is the web files. Age policy is 18+ by owner decision, so teen and parental controls are off by decision and not listed. Line numbers in code evidence come from the ledger and comparison files; I opened only PrivacySection.tsx, temporary-chat-policy.ts, config.rs, delete-account and export routes to confirm they exist.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both sell a ladder of individual plans, team seats and contract Enterprise, with web, Apple and Google billing, credits past plan limits, refunds, promotions and education programs. AGI has most of the web billing machinery built, behind a paid-upgrade waitlist the owner keeps on. Mobile sells nothing in v1. Main gaps: annual individual billing, gifts, wallet, education and verified-user programs, API credits, per-member admin budgets, and credit notes. All competitor facts reviewed 2026-11-22.
trace.scope_notes: All competitor evidence is from the 2026-11-22 catalogue (area 'Plans, billing and usage': 288 Claude-side and 355 ChatGPT-side lines). Claude means the chat product (support.claude.com, claude.com/pricing). Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool; it signs in with the same Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan and shares one usage pool with Claude chat, and an API key switches it to API billing. ChatGPT means help.openai.com and chatgpt.com pages. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com and some help.openai.com pages) is the separate coding tool; it is included in ChatGPT plans, shares one allowance pool with ChatGPT Work, and also signs in with an API key. Plan names in the catalogue are Claude Free/Pro/Max/Ultra/Team/Enterprise and ChatGPT Free/Go/Plus/Pro (three tiers)/Business/Enterprise/Edu. Many offers are US-only, region-limited or time-limited (teacher plans to 2028, student offer ended 2026-10-31); these limits are stated per capability. Model names are left out on purpose. AGI plan names come from packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts (labels Free, Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise; stored ids pro and max_15x differ from labels). Ledger briefs 81 and 83 still use older plan names (Max 5x, Max 15x); I used the code. Ledger line numbers can drift; recheck before citing.

trace.summary: Usage limits are mostly built for AGI's managed cloud on web, desktop and CLI. Mobile hides purchases by owner decision, and Chrome and VS Code send buying to the web. Gaps: auto-resume after a reset, a "now using credits" notice, per-member and group caps, admin requests for more usage, per-chat cost, and sharing the plan with outside apps. Web Free denial messages and Premium limit-denial paths were seen failing. Local mode behaviour is not documented.
trace.scope_notes: Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. Claude (chat on web, desktop, mobile) and Claude Code (terminal, IDE, Code tab) share ONE allowance per account on Pro, Max and Ultra: a five-hour window, a weekly window, and a separate weekly cap for the newest top-tier model family. Verified Ultra accounts have no five-hour window. Usage credits (pay as you go at API rates) extend past limits; Max and Ultra monthly API credits are separate and do not cover the apps or interactive Claude Code. Team and seat-based Enterprise use admin-controlled credits and spend limits. ChatGPT chat is described as unlimited text chat under abuse guardrails, with limited uploads, images, voice and research on lower plans. The measured allowances are mostly for Codex and ChatGPT Work (the coding and agent products), which share one pool with Excel, Word and PowerPoint add-ins: five-hour and weekly windows on Plus and Business Standard, a monthly allowance on Go, weekly only on Pro, credits beyond that, and one-time or banked resets. Codex pages describe the separate coding tool, but it signs in with the ChatGPT plan and shares its allowance. Claude Code pages describe the coding tool; it connects to Claude through the same plan allowance. Many items are Pro/Max/Ultra, Plus/Pro, Team/Enterprise or Business/Enterprise only; plans are noted per item. The catalogue does not show ChatGPT per-message chat caps for Plus beyond 'caps vary with demand'. AGI facts come from code reading (comparison CSVs, capability ledger area 82, docs/product) except where a scorecard or defect file says a person saw it. The AGI plan names (Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra) differ from competitor plan names.

trace.summary: Recovery is well documented by ChatGPT (retry in place, regenerate, kept drafts, delete is permanent, Library restore) and by Claude Code (resume, rewind, interrupt). The Claude chat catalogue is thin: error text and limits only. AGI has most of the behaviour in code. A person saw offline drafts, kept stopped answers and reload work on web. They also saw faults: a stale offline banner, a lost answer on reload, and a delete dialog that says "cannot be undone" while a 30-day restore exists. The CLI has gaps.
trace.scope_notes: Review date 2026-11-22. Claude (chat, support.claude.com) documents error messages, limits, capacity messages, length limits, and deleting a chat with a 30-day purge; it does not document retry, regenerate, offline behaviour or restore of deleted chats in the catalogue, so those are has: unknown. Claude Code (code.claude.com and its help articles) owns session resume, rewind and checkpoints, interrupts, and auto-continue of cut-off turns; these are a separate coding tool and are not evidence for the Claude chat app. ChatGPT (help.openai.com) documents error fixes, Regenerate, inline retry, draft saving, archive and permanent delete, Library Recently deleted, and iOS retry. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com) documents thread archive/unarchive, revert, steer, interrupt, queue; it is a separate coding tool that connects to ChatGPT through the same plan and shared chats in the desktop app. Plan limits: Claude limit messages vary by plan (five-hour and weekly limits, usage credits on paid plans); ChatGPT context-full notice is Free-plan; Library restore and search-regenerate are plan or workspace scoped. AGI facts come from QA comparison CSVs, the area-19 and area-88 ledgers, and code. Only the Web scorecards (2026-11-24) and the web problems file count as seen by a person; Desktop shows the hosted web app, so web evidence covers it only in part. Competitor columns in the AGI comparison CSVs were not used as evidence.

trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT document sign-in, verification, sessions, security and age rules in depth; Claude Code and Codex add terminal sign-in. AGI covers the common core on web: code, password, social, passkeys, authenticator, sessions, SSO and 18+. Gaps: no sign-in everywhere on CLI, VS Code and Chrome, no ID age check, no phone or push factors, no second account, no guest chat, and no admin sign-in limits.
trace.scope_notes: Evidence date for all competitor claims: 2026-11-22, from the saved catalogue only. Claude (support.claude.com) is the chat product: Google, emailed link and SSO sign-in, no password, 28-day web session, active sessions page, 18+ with Yoti or Persona age checks, phone verification at sign-up. Claude Code (code.claude.com) is the separate coding tool: browser login, /login, /logout, setup-token for CI, managed login restrictions, gateway SSO, cloud-provider credentials. It connects to the chat product because a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise claude.ai login is the main way in and the Free plan has no Claude Code access. ChatGPT (help.openai.com) is the chat product: password, Google, Microsoft, Apple, phone-only sign-up, MFA by app, push, SMS or passkey, Advanced Account Security, active sessions, two-account switcher, age prediction with Persona. Codex (learn.chatgpt.com/docs) is the separate coding tool: Sign in with ChatGPT or an API key, device code, access tokens, workspace locks; it shares the ChatGPT account. Plan limits: enterprise SSO, SCIM, admin sign-in locks and account-switching switches are Team, Business or Enterprise only; Advanced Account Security is documented for personal accounts on Free, Go, Plus and Pro. Many pages carry region limits (phone-only sign-up is rolling out in some regions; Italy age check). AGI line numbers below were checked on 2026-11-24 where given as path:line; comparison CSV line numbers drift, so rows cited only by file name were not re-checked. Sign-in is separate from payment: Local chat on mobile and desktop needs no account (requirements.md M-US-002 and decisions 2026-11-13), and Managed Free needs sign-in.

trace.summary: Both leaders document a deep admin layer: roles, SSO, SCIM, audit and compliance feeds, model and connector policy, spend limits, analytics, managed settings. AGI's ledger (code reading only) shows most of these built on Web, which Desktop shows, with Mobile partial. Gaps are required SSO, per-user and group spend limits, dynamic groups, MDM for the apps, support access, and finished data residency. No admin flow was seen working by a person.
trace.scope_notes: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-22. Claude (claude.ai) admin pages are on support.claude.com and claude.com: Team and Enterprise plans, Primary Owner, Owner, Admin, User and Enterprise custom roles. Claude Code is a separate coding tool; its admin pages (code.claude.com: managed settings, server-managed settings, self-hosted gateway) connect to Claude chat through the same organisation and admin console, and Team or Enterprise plans. ChatGPT admin pages are on help.openai.com (Business, Enterprise, Edu workspaces plus a tenant Admin Console). trace.summary: Claude and ChatGPT both ship desktop, phone, web and browser-extension apps plus separate coding tools, with OS hooks such as global shortcuts, widgets and deep links. AGI has a Mac-only signed desktop installer with auto-update, a Mac-only desktop shell, a script-installed CLI, store-ready phone and extension builds, and many OS hooks. Largest gaps: Windows and Linux desktop, update channels, managed-fleet controls, package-manager installs, Apple Intelligence, CarPlay, reading other apps. No item is seen working by a person.
trace.scope_notes: Claude (chat product) and Claude Code (coding tool) are documented on different sites. support.claude.com covers Claude Desktop, mobile apps, Claude in Chrome and the iOS and Android system hooks. code.claude.com covers the Claude Code CLI, its VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin, deep links and computer use from the terminal. They meet in the Claude Desktop app, which hosts Chat, Cowork and a Code tab, in claude:// links that open Code sessions, in the /mobile QR command, and in the Chrome extension that Claude Code and Desktop both use. ChatGPT and Codex are merged on desktop: learn.chatgpt.com says the new ChatGPT desktop app hosts Chat, Work and Codex (macOS and Windows, with a Linux preview), and the older Codex app moves into it. Codex CLI and the Codex IDE extension remain separate coding tools. Plan limits that matter: Claude Code and Cowork on Desktop need a paid plan; the Stable/Latest channel needs Desktop 4.29.0 or newer and is not on Linux, Store or IT-managed installs; Mac and Windows MSIX/PKG deployment pages are for Team and Enterprise; Windows ChatGPT app pages list Plus, Team, Edu, Enterprise; enterprise update controls are Enterprise and Edu; several iOS and Android items are All plans but Team and Enterprise lose location. Linux apps from both leaders are beta or preview. Review date for all competitor evidence: 2026-11-22. Catalogue rows are summaries; where a row is not shown, has is unknown. The project ledger (area briefs) and comparison CSVs disagree in places; code wins (AGENTS.md section 2) and each disagreement is flagged below.

Computer Use in the desktop app; macOS needs Screen Recording and Accessibility; runs in background on macOS and foreground on Windows; locked use continues after the Mac locks.

requirement.statement: Computer use asks for each OS permission with an explanation, lists allowed and refused apps, shows when it is acting, and always has Stop and Take over.

current.by_app: Desktop (Mac): computer use with Take over and Stop, permission status screen, allowed and refused app lists, tray stop. Missing: background mode, Locked Use, @Computer mention, admin per-app list.

capabilities.name: Deep links
capabilities.what_it_is: A custom link scheme opens the app on a chat, project, settings page or a new chat with a prefilled prompt.

claude.product: Claude (claude:// for Desktop and mobile); Claude Code (claude-cli://, vscode:// URI)

evidence.says: URL scheme launches the app if closed and opens a new chat (prefilled q up to about 14,000 characters), an existing chat or project.
claude-cli:// links open Claude Code with a prefilled prompt; shows a safety banner; handler registered on first interactive use; disableDeepLinkRegistration turns it off.
claude://code opens Code sessions in mobile apps; https links work as universal links.
codex:// deep links for chats, plugin-backed chats, Settings pages, Skills and Scheduled (catalogue rows cl06:223 to cl06:226).

requirement.statement: Links open the right screen from a cold start and from notifications; a link that carries a prompt shows it for review and never sends it by itself; admins can stop link registration.
requirement.source: docs/product/experience-contract.md and ledger S70.30 (links open the app on the right screen)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: A link never changes mode: a link cannot move a Local chat to Cloud or BYOK. It opens in the current mode and signed-in account.

current.by_app: Desktop: agiworkforce-cloud:// links open chats, projects, settings from cold start. No prefilled new-chat link (D94), no links to Skills or new schedule (DP102), no admin off switch (D96). CLI: no link scheme. VS Code: handoff links work; no prefilled-prompt link. Mobile: notification links work.

capabilities.gap: No prefilled-prompt links, no admin switch, no CLI links.
acceptance_criteria: A link opens the named chat when the app is closed.
A link with a prompt fills the composer and does not send.
A link cannot start a cloud send from a Local chat.

verification.evidence: Ledger done for S70.30; not run.

capabilities.name: iPhone widgets, Lock Screen control and Action button
capabilities.what_it_is: Home Screen widgets, a Lock Screen or Control Center control and an Action-button shortcut that open the phone app or start a task.

evidence.says: iOS 18+ widget with buttons to start a new chat, open dictation or take a photo; usage counts toward limits.
Open Claude control for the Lock Screen and Control Center; the Action button can launch it.
Feb 2025: ChatGPT as Safari default search and a home-screen widget (catalogue row oh08:369).

requirement.statement: Phone widgets and system controls open the app or start a new chat, camera or voice; a widget never shows chat content on a locked screen unless the user allowed it.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: A widget starts a chat in the user's current mode. In Local mode the chat uses the on-device model. A started chat counts in the one subscription.

current.by_app: Mobile: iPhone widget (small and medium) with New chat, Camera, Voice; one Open control for Lock Screen, Control Center and Action Button. Ledger S71.20 and S71.21 say missing; the code exists, so the ledger is stale. No Live Activity.

capabilities.gap: No Live Activity; no Analyze Photo control. Ledger rows need correcting.
acceptance_criteria: Add the widget; each button opens the right screen.
Add the Lock Screen control on iOS 18 and open the app.
Widget buttons work with no network in Local mode.

verification.evidence: Swift file exists at cited path; not seen on a device.

capabilities.name: Android widget, icon shortcuts and default assistant
capabilities.what_it_is: An Android home widget, long-press app shortcuts, a selected-text menu entry and an optional default-assistant role.

evidence.says: Resizable widget on Android 8.0+ with buttons for new chat, camera capture and voice dictation; usage counts toward limits.

requirement.statement: Android has a widget and icon shortcuts; a default-assistant role is optional.
requirement.source: competitor parity (widget); default assistant not documented by either leader in the catalogue
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Assist gesture or widget starts a chat in the current mode; microphone permission is asked with an explanation.

current.by_app: Mobile: widget with New chat, Camera, Voice; long-press icon shortcuts; Process text menu entry. No default-assistant role and no Quick Settings tile (S71.24 missing).

capabilities.gap: No assistant role or tile; ledger S71.20 stale.
acceptance_criteria: Add the widget; Voice opens dictation and asks for the microphone once.
Long-press the icon; New chat opens a chat.
Select text in another app; Process text offers AGI.

verification.evidence: Files exist; not run on a device.

capabilities.name: Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight and Apple Intelligence
capabilities.what_it_is: Using the assistant through the iPhone system: Shortcuts actions, Siri phrases, Spotlight and Apple Intelligence hand-off.

evidence.says: On iOS 18+ users can ask Claude from Spotlight, Siri, the Share menu or any intent-aware app without opening the app; the Ask intent uses the default model and counts toward usage.
Ask Siri to use ChatGPT, use Compose in Writing Tools, or Visual Intelligence; works without an account or with a free or paid account.

requirement.statement: Shortcuts and Siri actions run a chat and count in usage. Apple Intelligence integration is a product choice.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: An intent that runs without opening the app must use the user's default mode and model, and must refuse to send to Cloud when Local is selected and no local model is ready.

current.by_app: Mobile: eight App Shortcuts (Ask, Summarize, Analyze Image, Transcribe, Translate, Scan and more); Ask runs without opening the app. No Writing Tools or Visual Intelligence, no Apple Intelligence extension. Desktop: no Siri integration.

capabilities.gap: No Apple Intelligence integration. Ledger S71.23 says not applicable but shortcuts exist.
acceptance_criteria: Say Ask AGI to Siri; an answer returns without opening the app.
In Local mode with no model downloaded the intent says so rather than using Cloud.
Each shortcut appears in the Shortcuts app.

capabilities.name: Phone system apps: calendar, reminders, location, messages
capabilities.what_it_is: The assistant reads or creates calendar events and reminders, drafts messages, and uses location, with permission prompts.

evidence.says: Drafts texts and emails, reads the calendar and creates events, creates reminders, finds nearby places on a map; Team and Enterprise lack location; cannot read messages or contacts.
Android drafts messages, reads the calendar, sets alarms and timers; reminders exist only on iOS.
Device location sharing with a separate precise-location toggle (catalogue row oh08:284).

requirement.statement: Each phone tool asks for the OS permission when first used, shows what will be written before it is written, and keeps data on the device unless the user sends it.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Calendar or reminder content read by a tool is sent to the model only on a Cloud or BYOK turn and the label says which. In Local mode it goes to the on-device model only. Needs a model with tool use; say so when the chosen model cannot.

current.by_app: Mobile: Cloud chat can read the calendar or add a confirmed event, and add a confirmed reminder on iPhone. No message drafting, alarms, location, contacts or health data.

capabilities.gap: Message drafting, alarms, location and Maps, health data.
acceptance_criteria: Ask to add an event; a permission prompt and a confirmation appear before it is created.
Deny the permission; the app explains and does nothing.
In Local mode the tool is shown as unavailable or runs on device only.

verification.evidence: Comparison rows only; the path in current.evidence is a prefix from the comparison row and I did not open it.

capabilities.name: Share-sheet intake
capabilities.what_it_is: Sharing text, links, images or files from another app opens the assistant with that content.

evidence.says: The Ask intent can be used from the Share menu on iOS 18+.
Share photos or content to your dot via the iOS share sheet (catalogue row cl02:125).

requirement.statement: Sharing from any app opens a preview that starts a chat with the shared item.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: The shared item goes only to the chosen model route; the preview shows the mode. In Local mode it stays on device.

current.by_app: Mobile: iOS share extension and Android SEND targets for text, links, images, PDFs.

capabilities.gap: none known
acceptance_criteria: Share a link from Safari; AGI opens with a preview and a Start chat button.
Share a PDF; it attaches and the model can read it or says it cannot.

capabilities.what_it_is: Voice chat inside the car system (CarPlay or Android Auto).

evidence.says: Voice-first ChatGPT in CarPlay on supported iPhones with iOS 26.4 or later: start a new voice chat, start one inside a project, or resume a recent chat.

requirement.statement: Not required today. If built, voice-only, minimal driver distraction, no screen content.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Needs a voice-capable model route; Local mode would need local speech; say so.

current.by_app: Mobile: no CarPlay or Android Auto; ledger S109.14 says not applicable.
evidence: searched: CarPlay, CPTemplate in apps/mobile (per comparison M145)

capabilities.gap: Not built by design or not decided.
acceptance_criteria: If built: start a voice chat from the car display with no typing.

capabilities.name: Office and workspace add-ins
capabilities.what_it_is: Installing the assistant inside another vendor's product such as Word or Google Docs.

evidence.says: Install from Workspace Marketplace yourself, or a super admin installs for everyone or allowlists the app; Chrome, Edge, Safari supported, not Firefox.
Sidebar from Microsoft Marketplace to draft, summarize and revise; works on the open document only; separate from chat history, memory and skills.
evidence.plans: Free, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu

requirement.statement: Not a stated requirement. Decide whether add-ins belong in the six-app scope.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: An add-in would be a cloud surface under the one subscription; no Local mode; the document text goes to the chosen route and the add-in must say so.

current.by_app: None of the six apps ships an Office or Workspace add-in; not examined in the comparison rows I read.

capabilities.gap: Outside current six-app scope.
acceptance_criteria: If built: install from the vendor marketplace and use it on the open document.

capabilities.name: Launch at login and background behaviour
capabilities.what_it_is: The desktop app can start at login, keep running in the background, stay awake for long tasks and react to sleep and lock.

evidence.says: Locked Use continues Computer Use after the Mac locks (a lock-state behaviour; no launch-at-login row in the catalogue).

requirement.statement: The user can start the app at login, see and control background activity, and long tasks survive sleep or pause with a clear message.
requirement.source: docs/product/definition.md (desktop settings include run on startup and keep computer awake)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Background work in Local mode must not send data out; background cloud work must show it is on our servers.

current.by_app: Desktop: launch at login and background controls done; sleep, wake and lock handling missing (S70.32).

capabilities.gap: No sleep, wake or lock handling; quit confirmation covers less than the row asks.
acceptance_criteria: Turn on start at login; reboot; the app starts hidden or visible as set.
Lock the screen during a task; the app pauses or continues as documented and says which.

capabilities.name: Hardware controls and macropads
capabilities.what_it_is: A physical keyboard, button or macropad that triggers assistant actions.

chatgpt.product: ChatGPT desktop with Codex (Codex Micro keyboard)

evidence.says: Codex Micro keyboard with the ChatGPT desktop app: USB-C or Bluetooth, agent keys with status lights, push-to-talk microphone key (catalogue rows cl05:144 to cl05:153).

requirement.statement: No requirement. Hardware keys are an owner choice.
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Keys would trigger the same actions as shortcuts; no model dependence.

current.by_app: Mobile: iPhone Action Button works through the Open control; Desktop: no hardware keyboard support.

capabilities.gap: Desktop hardware not built; decision pending.
acceptance_criteria: If built: pairing shows the device and a key press runs the mapped action.

capabilities.name: Local model install and storage on the device
capabilities.what_it_is: Downloading, sizing, loading and deleting on-device models, with hardware readiness shown. AGI has this; the leaders' catalogue rows show no equivalent.

requirement.statement: Free local inference on mobile and desktop: the app shows installed, downloadable, unavailable and runtime-offline states, lets the user download, pause, delete and load models, and shows device readiness. Fresh install with no model shows setup guidance.
requirement.source: docs/product/requirements.md (M-ONB-003, M-MODEL-002; fresh install with no local model shows setup guidance)
requirement.fit_with_models_providers_subscription: Runs without payment and, per owner decisions, sign-in is a separate matter. No Local prompt or file may be silently sent to BYOK or Managed Cloud (AGENTS.md section 6). Models come from the generated catalog, not from literals in the app.

current.by_app: Mobile: download manager, storage manager, hardware panel, load and unload, runtime health done. Desktop: local model management marked not applicable (S70.23), though the desktop runtime has local-model code. CLI and VS Code: no model manager. No hybrid local-to-cloud approval flow (S109.23, S109.24 missing).

capabilities.gap: Desktop local model management and explicit cloud-escalation approval are missing.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh phone install with no model, the app offers a download and then answers a prompt offline.
Delete a model; storage use drops and the model shows downloadable.
A Local chat never sends a message to Cloud without a visible consent step.

verification.evidence: Ledger done for mobile; not run by a person.

unresolved_product_choices: Whether the public Desktop ships for Windows and Linux, and in what order; today only Mac builds.
Whether to offer a Stable/Latest channel (only Claude documents it) on desktop, CLI and VS Code.
Whether to match enterprise fleet controls (MSIX, PKG, MDM keys, minimum version, in-app update switch) both leaders document for paid enterprise plans.
Whether to build Apple Intelligence integration, CarPlay or Android Auto, and a hardware keyboard (each documented by ChatGPT only).
Whether to read text from the front app (ChatGPT Work with Apps) and whether Claude-style background computer use is wanted.
Whether to offer an installable web app and offline fallback; the manifest exists but the ledger marks both not applicable.
Whether the CLI is offered through Homebrew, WinGet, apt, dnf and npm as the leaders do, or only by the signed script.
Whether a managed Intune-style phone build and Office or Workspace add-ins are in scope.
Whether the Android default-assistant role and Quick Settings tile are wanted.
Whether the update check, an outside call, is allowed by default in a strict Local setup.
could_not_establish: Whether any installer, store listing, Chrome Web Store page or CLI release is publicly live today: sources say not published, and I did not check release APIs or run anything.
No person-seen result covers install, update or OS integration: the web scorecard and defect list cover browser chat flows only.

The ledger and code disagree on phone widgets (S71.20, S71.21 say missing; Swift and Kotlin widget files exist), on Siri and shortcuts (S71.23) and on installable web (S69.14); I did not run any app to settle them.

Claude Desktop Windows installer details beyond the MSIX deploy page were not opened; several catalogue rows (Quick entry screenshot, Appshots hotkeys, codex:// deep links, Codex Micro) were taken from the row text without opening the saved page.
Whether Claude has global shortcut, menu bar, launch-at-login or default-assistant behaviour beyond Mac quick entry: the catalogue shows no row, so has is unknown.
Minimum iOS version of the AGI phone app is unverified.
I did not open code for the phone-system tools path; it is quoted from the comparison row.
Whether the retained Tauri build is expected to be migrated to Electron for existing users: no source.
